summary: Teotihuacan is a dense, multi-layered worker-placement game where dice act as your workers and grow in value as you use them, forcing constant tension between advancing dice and needing lower numbers for cheaper actions. Every turn is a puzzle of optimizing a tight engine across temples, technology, houses, and the central pyramid, with the game periodically resetting resources at era-end scoring.
praised: Dice-as-workers mechanic feels fresh and creates a unique 'value vs. utility' puzzle
Deep, tightly interlocking systems with satisfying engine-building
High replayability from modular board and variable setup
criticised: Steep learning curve and heavy rulebook overhead for new players
Can feel solitary/multiplayer-solitaire with limited direct interaction
Analysis paralysis due to many simultaneous considerations
Iconography and initial onboarding seen as unintuitive
Theme feels pasted on top of a heavily Euro-style mechanism set

interaction.kind: Mostly parallel play with some space/tile competition and area denial on the shared board

scoring.why: Fame comes from multiple systems (temples, pyramid layers, technology, houses, resources at reset) so the winner is usually whoever balances the most engines efficiently across all three eras
